records.context: Julio checks Rafael is following before walking him through Deck View. He starts with the captain, then describes the jobs that keep a ship moving and which sailors help with navigation, observation and negotiations. An anonymous system panel tells the player how to open the screen.
records.Japanese:
ここまでは大丈夫かのう？
さて、これからは航海士のこと、つまり
わしらのことについて教えよう
records.source_meaning: Julio checks whether Rafael has understood, then turns to what people like Julio do aboard ship.
records.localization_note: Keep his friendly check-in and shift to the ship's crew, including Julio.
records.english: Still with me? Now let me show you what the crew does aboard ship.
records.previous_English: Still with me? I'll show you what we do as navigators.

records.Japanese:
提督の大事な仕事のひとつに
『人事』というものがある
records.source_meaning: An admiral is responsible for assigning people to their duties.
records.localization_note: His plain explanation preserves the distinction between the admiral and the captain.
records.english: One of an admiral's main jobs is assigning duties.

records.Japanese:
航海を快適に行うために
それぞれ航海士の担当を決める
わけじゃな
実際に甲板を見ながら行うのじゃ
records.source_meaning: Giving each crew member a duty helps the voyage go smoothly. Julio is about to demonstrate this on the Deck screen.
records.localization_note: Make the instruction lead naturally into the demonstration and keep the exact menu label.
records.english: Give everyone a job so the voyage goes smoothly. Let's make those assignments in Deck View.
records.previous_English: Give each navigator a job so the voyage goes smoothly. Let's do that in Deck View.

records.speaker: Julio Erneco

records.Japanese:
まず、艦長はFIじゃ
艦長がいないと船はうごかん
勝手にどこかへ行くわけにはいかん
からのう
records.source_meaning: Rafael is the captain. Without a captain a ship stays put. It cannot pick a destination on its own.
records.localization_note: Julio identifies Rafael directly, then repeats why the ship needs a captain. Keep the two reasons and the light joke. The four complete sentences fit all tested given-name widths.
records.english: First up is the captain. That's you, FI. A ship needs a captain to sail. It can't set a course on its own.
records.previous_English: First, you're the captain, FI. A ship can't sail without a captain. It can't choose where to go on its own.
protected_phrases: A ship needs a captain to sail.
It can't set a course on its own.

records.speaker: Julio Erneco

records.Japanese:
次は、操帆手じゃな
風に対して帆の角度を調節してくれる
マストの数と同じだけの操帆手が
必要じゃ
records.source_meaning: The Sail Handler adjusts the sails relative to the wind. The ship needs one per mast.
records.localization_note: Keep the job name, the angle of the sails relative to the wind and the per-mast staffing rule. Each of Julio's instructions can finish in the same row.
records.english: Next is the Sail Handler. They angle the sails for the wind. You'll need one for each mast.
records.previous_English: Next is the Sail Handler. They adjust the sails' angle to the wind. Each mast needs one.
protected_phrases: They angle the sails for the wind.
You'll need one for each mast.

records.Japanese:
それから、操舵手じゃ
船を速く回頭させたいなら重要になって
くるぞい
records.source_meaning: The Helmsman is especially important when the ship needs to turn quickly.
records.localization_note: The direct advice gives the role its practical purpose and sets up the battle example.
records.english: To turn the ship quickly, count on your Helmsman.
records.previous_English: To turn the ship quickly, count on your Helmsman.

records.Japanese:
海戦の時でも、操舵手が優秀じゃと
船を素早く、有利な位置に
持っていくことができるように
なるわけじゃ
records.source_meaning: A skilled Helmsman can move the ship quickly into a favorable position in a sea battle.
records.localization_note: The concrete battle example explains why the Helmsman matters. It keeps speed and positioning distinct.
records.english: A skilled helmsman can quickly maneuver the ship into a favorable position in battle.
records.previous_English: A skilled helmsman can quickly maneuver the ship into a favorable position in battle.

records.Japanese:
それから、副官。いなくても船は
動くのじゃが、いれば、他勢力と交渉が
できるし、航海中、みんなが疲れにくく
なる。縁の下の力持ちじゃな
records.source_meaning: A ship can sail without a First Mate. Assigning one enables talks with other factions and slows fatigue during a voyage. The contribution is easily overlooked.
records.localization_note: Keep the two benefits, use the established faction term and preserve Julio's affectionate aside.
records.english: A First Mate is optional. They let you negotiate with other factions and keep the crew from tiring as fast at sea. An unsung hero.
records.previous_English: A First Mate is optional, but lets you negotiate with other powers and keeps the crew from tiring so fast at sea. An unsung hero.

records.Japanese:

艦隊の緯度経度が分かるようになる

records.source_meaning: A Surveyor lets the fleet use Auto Move and see its latitude and longitude. Julio calls the work important.
records.localization_note: It names both benefits clearly and sounds like Julio explaining a job he respects.
records.english: With a Surveyor, you can use Auto Move and see the fleet's latitude and longitude. It's an important job.
records.previous_English: With a Surveyor, you can use Auto Move and see the fleet's latitude and longitude. It's an important job.

records.english: At sea, the Lookout tells you who other ships belong to and what's happening in nearby towns.
